$comment: Known, accepted npm audit advisories at high/critical severity.
Checked by scripts/audit-check.mjs, which FAILS CI on any high/critical
advisory NOT listed here — so new vulnerabilities break the build while
these known ones do not.
Every entry needs a reason and a reviewBy date. Entries that no longer
match anything are reported as stale so they get deleted rather than
silently widening the exception over time.
Phase 3B (Expo SDK 54 -> 57) cleared the four earlier entries (image-size x2,
postcss x2), which the gate then reported as stale and they were removed.
2026-10-12: the two entries below have NO patched release (latest braces 3.0.3
and node-forge 1.4.0 are the vulnerable versions) and are reached only through
build/dev tooling, never the deployed server or the apps. Re-check by reviewBy;
once a fixed version ships, `npm update braces node-forge` and delete the entry.
The same day, http-cache-semantics, shell-quote and source-map-js were fixed by
a lockfile-only update.
The 14 findings that remain are all MODERATE and therefore below this
gate's threshold. They sit in @expo/* build tooling and expo-router's
query-string/decode-uri-component chain at the latest published SDK, so
there is no version to upgrade to; npm's suggested 'fixes' for them are
downgrades to expo@46 / expo-router@5 and are not real.

allow.reason: Stack-exhaustion DoS from deeply nested brace patterns. No patched version exists (<=3.0.3 = latest). Reached only via micromatch in Expo/Metro's file watcher and chokidar under ts-node-dev (local dev server); patterns come from our own config, never from users, and none of it runs in the deployed server (node dist/) or the apps.

RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signature forgery with low-exponent keys. No patched version exists (<=1.4.0 = latest). Reached only via @expo/cli and @expo/code-signing-certificates (Expo Updates code signing on a developer machine); we don't use Expo Updates code signing, and nothing at runtime loads node-forge.
